report_name: Phishing Attacks Abusing Legitimate RMM Tools Surge by 475%

attack_patterns.name: Remote Access Software
attack_patterns.description: Attackers abused legitimate Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tools like ScreenConnect and AnyDesk for malicious remote control over victim systems after a social engineering lure.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: The initial access vector for the phishing campaign was a link in an email that led victims to a malicious payload delivery chain.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing via Service
attack_patterns.description: Attackers abused Microsoft Power BI domains to host the initial lure, adding a layer of legitimacy and helping to evade security filters.

attack_patterns.name: User Execution
attack_patterns.description: The attack relies on social engineering to convince the victim to run the downloaded portable RMM installer and grant access to the attacker.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
attack_patterns.description: An attacker-controlled website used a JavaScript to programmatically trigger the download of a rogue ScreenConnect installer after a time delay.

attack_patterns.name: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion
attack_patterns.description: Attackers employed a time-delay tactic on their payload website to evade automated sandboxes before initiating the malware download.

attack_patterns.name: Time Based Checks
attack_patterns.description: A script on the attacker's website initiated the payload download only after a few seconds had passed, a method used to bypass automated analysis environments.

tools.name: ScreenConnect
tools.description: A legitimate RMM tool abused by attackers to gain remote control over victim machines. A rogue, portable installer for ScreenConnect was delivered via a phishing campaign that leveraged Microsoft Power BI domains.

tools.name: AnyDesk
tools.description: A legitimate RMM tool used in widespread phishing campaigns to gain remote access to victim systems through social engineering.

campaigns.name: Power BI RMM Phishing Campaign
campaigns.description: A phishing campaign first observed on September 10, 2026, that abused Microsoft Power BI domains to host lures which led to the download of a rogue ScreenConnect installer. The campaign used time-delay tactics to evade sandboxes.

identities.name: North American financial institutions
identities.description: The primary target sector for the surge of phishing attacks abusing RMM tools in 2026.

infrastructure.name: Attacker-controlled payload website
infrastructure.description: A website used to fingerprint the victim's system, employ a time-delay for sandbox evasion, and trigger the download of a rogue RMM installer.

indicators.name: Legitimate RMM Tool Execution
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Legitimate RMM Tool Execution
id: 7c8b1a2d-3e4f-4a9b-8c1d-2e3f4a5b6c7d
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of legitimate RMM tools like ScreenConnect or AnyDesk, which are often abused in phishing campaigns.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/threatsday-ransomware-affiliate.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-08
tags:
  - attack.t1219
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\ScreenConnect.Client.exe'
      - '\AnyDesk.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of RMM client binaries, especially if initiated by a browser or email client.

indicators.name: Outbound RMM Network Traffic
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Outbound RMM Network Traffic
id: 8d9c2b3e-4f5a-4b0c-9d2e-3f4a5b6c7d8e
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS queries for known RMM tool domains like ScreenConnect or AnyDesk. Such traffic from unauthorized workstations can indicate malicious activity.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/threatsday-ransomware-affiliate.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-08
tags:
  - attack.t1219
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|endswith:
      - '.screenconnect.com'
      - '.anydesk.com'
      - '.relay.anydesk.com'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects network connections to known RMM relay servers from user workstations that do not normally use these tools.

indicators.name: Browser or Email Client Spawning RMM Tool
indicators.pattern:
title: Browser or Email Client Spawning RMM Tool
id: 9e0d3c4f-5a6b-4c1d-8e3f-4a5b6c7d8e9f
status: experimental
description: Detects a web browser or email client spawning a remote management (RMM) tool process, which is a strong indicator of a social engineering attack.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/threatsday-ransomware-affiliate.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-08
tags:
  - attack.t1219
  - attack.t1566.002
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\iexplore.exe'
      - '\outlook.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\ScreenConnect.Client.exe'
      - '\AnyDesk.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects suspicious process chains, such as a web browser or Office application spawning an RMM client process.

relationships.source_name: Browser or Email Client Spawning RMM Tool
